headline: No documented interaction pathway; both open-source agents are network-isolated and lack shared I/O surfaces, so pairwise risks are minimal.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent exposes a shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or permissive parser in the profiles. Agent A has no I/O surfaces and agent B likewise shows no I/O surfaces; with no documented bridge, prompt injection between them is not plausible from the available evidence.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not add shared clipboard or message-queue bridges.
Review any future parser that consumes peer output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles show no data classes touched, no shared workspace, and no network egress for either agent. Without a shared storage or upload path, there is no plausible route for one agent to leak the other's data.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent gains outbound network access, reassess exfiltration risk.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Confirm outbound network remains disabled.
Separate credentials and local profiles.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles lack write surfaces, concurrency details, and mutable resource scopes. Agent A is game-playing and agent B is travel-planning, but neither is documented to write files, modify git state, or share OAuth scopes, so no capability conflict is evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same directory or mutable service, conflict risk becomes possible.
IF the orchestrator adds shared locks or shared state, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Do not grant overlapping service credentials.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no evidence that agent B consumes agent A's outputs as authoritative, and neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority. With no documented output-to-input chain, cascading error is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF agent B is configured to trust agent A's outputs without verification, reassess.
IF either agent is connected to an action-taking toolchain, cascading impact may emerge.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action.
Require explicit validation of peer outputs.
Keep both agents disconnected from actuators.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent messages.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, retention, certification, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Agent A and agent B both show empty data_classes_touched, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later assigned to either agent, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention policies diverge for the same data class, reassess.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Record residency and retention policies.
Avoid routing regulated data until policies are defined.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
